title: You Must Cling to Your College Friends
author: Drunk Wisconsin
summary: The pseudonymous writer Drunk Wisconsin argues that, because making friends gets harder with age, people should hold tightly to the friends they made in college. He describes a seven-year run of annual camping trips, canoe outings and monthly gatherings with his friend group, and credits staying close to those friends with leading him to his wife and family. He draws on earlier writing that the best way to meet a partner after college is through friends, and says friendship is the real answer to the loneliness epidemic. Shared history, such as who showed up at a funeral or a hard diagnosis, makes existing friends hard to deprioritize. He notes that his family chooses where to live by closeness to friends, whose children have known each other from birth, and advises young people not to move away or to move where their friends are going. For those who lost touch, he urges them to reach out and reconnect. This piece was linked in Aaron Renn's 10.16.26 digest.
points: Adult friendship is hard to start, and loneliness is tied to the failure to date, marry and form families, so friendship is the practical remedy.
Friends are the best route to a spouse after college because each friend introduces you to coworkers, neighbors and cousins.
Long-standing friends are the ones present for deaths, diagnoses and illness, which makes loyalty to them rational rather than closed-minded.
Choosing a home near friends, whose children grow up together, builds a village that does not depend on relatives.
Young adults should weigh an extra ten thousand dollars a year against losing face-to-face contact, and those who drifted should reach out and reconnect.
quotes: Friendship is the real solution to the loneliness epidemic that’s sending many in our society down a dark life path.

Outside of online dating, the best way to meet potential partners is through friends. Your friends are able to introduce you to their coworkers, their neighbors, their cousins, and other new people they meet.
Who was there when someone’s mom died? Who attended the funeral? Who was there when their kid was diagnosed with a serious disability?
I’ve seen young, wild boys who make mistakes turn into mature men who don’t stop working from sunrise to sunset to provide for their families.
They know all their medical history better than a pediatrician reading MyChart. I’m not abandoning that for anything. I have my village already, and almost none of the villagers are related to me.
Don’t move away, or if you do, move to where your friends are moving to. Talk to them and discuss this exact dynamic.
Sometimes you finally meet up with someone you haven’t seen in years and find that you pick up right where you left off.
That is why I say you must cling, cling to your college friends as if life is trying to strip them away from your grasp, because it kind of is.
